bullets.title: FTC + 20 states file major antitrust suit against Amazon over ad price manipulation
bullets.body: The FTC, joined by 20+ state AGs, is filing a complaint in Seattle federal court alleging Amazon deceived advertisers and manipulated ad prices on its retail platform, reaping 'tens of billions of dollars' in excess profits over seven years. This is characterized as Amazon's third major antitrust case; the company previously settled a Prime signup lawsuit for $2.5B.

bullets.title: Trump weighing limited strikes on Iran over Hormuz — geopolitical risk spike
bullets.body: Multiple wires flagged that President Trump is weighing limited military strikes against Iran with the U.S. seeking to prevent Iran from rebuilding capabilities. Escalation around the Strait of Hormuz carries implications for energy prices and defense sector positioning.

bullets.title: Tom Lee: Markets could rally 'very strongly' if Fed holds in September
bullets.body: Fundstrat's Tom Lee, via CNBC's Squawk, argued that a Fed hold at the September meeting could catalyze a strong equity market rally. The comment comes as macro uncertainty keeps investors cautious into month-end.

bullets.title: OpenAI 'Jalapeño' custom chip removes L2 cache to slash inference latency
bullets.body: Commentary flags that OpenAI's custom AI chip, codenamed Jalapeño, removes the L2 cache as an architectural choice to cut inference latency, overcoming prior token throughput losses. The move signals OpenAI is deepening its vertical integration into silicon to optimize its inference stack.

bullets.title: JPMorgan trading desk turns tactically cautious after bullish 2026 call paid off
bullets.body: JPMorgan's trading desk, credited with 'perfectly timing the market in 2026,' has shifted its stance from bullish to tactically cautious. The desk's repositioning could be a meaningful near-term signal given the desk's recent track record.

bullets.title: Trump administration to sharply reduce vehicle fuel economy standards
bullets.body: Transportation Secretary Duffy is set to announce a rollback of vehicle fuel economy (CAFE) standards, a policy shift with implications for automakers and EV adoption trajectories.
